Boryslav Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. According to Yizkor Borislav, this cemetery was founded in 1886 on land donated by David Lindenbaum, making its origin more precisely documented than most in this collection. It closed in 1913 — notably before WWII — and some of its gravestones were relocated to the Jewish section of Boryslav's municipal cemetery. The broader Jewish community here grew enormous on the strength of the local oil industry, reaching nearly 13,000 by 1939, before Nazi occupation from July 1941 brought pogroms, mass executions, and deportations to Belzec that left only a few hundred survivors by war's end.
